items.title: The name
items.text: KBToysverse, an online shop founded by two former KB store employees, sells new KB Toys collectibles and says it operates “under a licensing agreement with the owners of the KB Toys® brand.”[^34] We could not confirm the current registrant from trademark records.

items.title: The 2018 comeback
items.text: Strategic Marks announced 1,000 pop-up stores for Christmas 2018, then 400 to 600, then a delay to 2019.[^31][^32] In March 2019 its founder said the money had not been raised.[^33]

items.title: The stores
items.text: All 461 were closed in going-out-of-business sales that began in December 2008.[^24] The company had 10,850 employees at the filing, about 6,500 of them seasonal.[^24]

items.title: Pittsfield
items.text: The headquarters at 100 West Street planned to lay off 240 of its 270 employees between the filing and February 2009.[^24] A former mayor of nearby North Adams was still telling the story on the campaign trail in 2012.[^26]

items.title: The seller’s note
items.text: Big Lots valued its $45M note at $13.2M on the day of the sale and at $7.3M after the 2004 bankruptcy. It was also left with guarantee or indemnification obligations on about 390 KB store leases.[^6]

items.title: The lawsuits
items.text: A Delaware judge dismissed Big Lots’ suit against Bain and former KB executives on March 28, 2006.[^7] The creditors’ claims over the 2002 payout were settled; the terms were not disclosed.[^25][^28]

blocks.title: Who has owned the name
blocks.subtitle: Six owners of the business, then three of the trademark.

nodes.what: Kaufman Brothers, a candy company in Pittsfield, becomes Kay-Bee, a toy retailer.[^35][^36]
Buys a chain of 210 stores and grows it past 1,000.[^36]
Buys 1,042 stores and renames the chain KB.[^1]
A leveraged buyout. The seller books a $430.8M after-tax loss.[^5]
Files after the 2003 price war and closes more than 600 stores.[^6][^24]
An affiliate pays for 90% of the stock of the reorganized company.[^20]
Buys the brand, website and trademarks through a subsidiary, CE Stores.[^29]
Registers the trademark after Toys “R” Us lets it expire in June 2016.[^30]
Sells KB Toys branded collectibles online. No stores.[^34]

blocks.source: Sources as cited on each step. The $2.1M figure is from press reports repeated by MassLive[^30]. The price paid by Strategic Marks, if any, is unknown.
